header.demoExplanation: The NASA data service is not connected, so this investigation uses precomputed educational sample data. It is not a live satellite observation.
header.liveExplanation: The API is connected and can retrieve current NASA AppEEARS satellite data.

home.description: Investigate urban heat islands using 8-day MODIS satellite composites.
home.illustration: Illustration of Earth and its climate data
home.step1Description: Pick a city on the globe or search for it. We pair it with a rural reference point about 45 km away.
home.step2Description: MODIS provides 8-day land-surface temperature composites for the city and rural reference area.
home.step3Description: Compare the curves and indicators to understand what the observations reveal.
home.disclaimer: Surface temperature is not air temperature, and correlation alone does not prove causation.
home.byTeam: A climate investigation by Team Zénith

results.noneDescription: Choose a city to compare its surface temperature with a rural reference point.
results.annualRateHelp: The slope of the trend calculated from annual averages to limit seasonal influence.
results.heatIslandHelp: Average difference in observed surface temperatures between the city and the rural reference point.
results.pValueHelp: A p-value below 0.05 is statistical evidence of a trend, not proof of causation.
results.rSquaredHelp: R² indicates how well the linear trend describes the observed annual averages.
results.annualSubtitle: City and rural reference · annual averages and trend
results.monthlySubtitle: City and rural reference · seasonal cycles across 8-day composites
results.projectionBase: Linear projection · compared with the {year} average
results.projectionUnavailable: This older result does not include projections. Run the investigation again to generate projections through 2100.
results.projectionWarning: Mathematical extrapolation at a constant rate (y = ax + b), not a certain forecast. The projection follows the annual trend.
results.longProjectionWarning: Mathematical extrapolation at a constant rate (y = ax + b). Uncertainty increases over the long term: real change will also depend on urban planning (greening, materials) and climate policies.
results.chooseAnnual: Choose “Annual trend” to display the projected zone and curves on the chart.
results.significantSummary: In {city}, the observed trend is statistically significant (p {p}). The urban surface is warming by an average of {slope} °C/year, while the average difference from the rural area is {gap} °C.
results.notSignificantSummary: For {city}, the data do not establish a statistically significant annual trend over this period (p {p}). This does not mean that no change is occurring.
results.scienceNote: Satellites observe the surface, not air temperature. A statistical trend does not prove a cause.
